rationale: A wins because its angles are more usable as assignments, especially "Klarna says its bot resolves a chat in under two minutes. Contact centers now have a number to beat," which gives a trade reporter a real benchmark instead of a fog machine. B has strong bones, but "When your BNPL dispute is decided by a chatbot" asserts the very fact its own proof list admits is unknown. A also nicks itself with "how many people lost their jobs," but it handles the disclosure problem more honestly across the angle and sends the founder to pick one lane; B wanders off to `newsjack-detector` as if the fresh update were not already the peg.
gaps_in_A: "It won't say how many people lost their jobs" overstates the supplied fact; the update says Klarna will not split roles cut versus left unfilled, not that confirmed people lost jobs.
"a chatbot may be the first one to rule on it" is a loaded adjudication frame; the supplied fact only says advocates raised concerns about AI handling disputes.
"The update is fresh" needs a harder date peg. With a June 9, 2026 current time, tie why-now to the actual announcement timing if available.
gaps_in_B: "When your BNPL dispute is decided by a chatbot" invents adjudication; the facts do not say the assistant decides disputes or handles chargebacks.
"Klarna cut average chat resolution from 11 minutes to under 2 - here's how" promises an implementation story the update does not supply; the proof list then asks for the missing how.
"No current news signal was supplied" is too cautious to the point of misreading the brief; the update itself says Klarna now reports the metrics as of June 9, 2026.
"Next step: newsjack-detector" is the wrong handoff for a founder with four usable angles; they need to choose a lane and fill proof holes, not restart discovery.
